learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears.

items.title: Starting check: center with an outlier
items.prompt: A sample has values 4, 5, 5, 6, and 30. Which statistic best describes a typical value without being pulled strongly by 30?

items.title: Guided practice: read center and range
items.prompt: A table lists trial times of 10, 12, 12, and 14 seconds. Which pair correctly reports the mean and range?

items.title: Less help: identify mode and middle spread
items.prompt: For values 2, 2, 3, 4, 5, 5, 5, and 9, which statement is supported?

items.title: Solo practice: compare dispersion
items.prompt: Groups A and B have the same mean. A has standard deviation 2 units and B has standard deviation 7 units. Which statement is supported?
options: A has the larger range for certain
B is more dispersed around the mean

items.title: Near exit: state the displayed pattern
items.prompt: A line graph shows concentration falling from 18 to 11 to 7 micromoles per liter across three successive time points. Which conclusion stays within the display?
options: Every future value will be below 7

items.title: Changed exit: choose summaries for skew
items.prompt: A salary list is strongly right-skewed because two values are much larger than the rest. Which pair best summarizes typical salary and middle-half spread?

items.title: Repair: separate center from spread
items.prompt: For values 3, 6, 6, 9, and 11, which calculation gives the range?

items.title: Fresh re-entry: summarize new values
items.prompt: A new data set is 6, 7, 7, 8, and 12. Which statement is correct?

items.title: Repair: match display to question
items.prompt: A researcher needs to show how one variable changes at six ordered time points. Which display best preserves that pattern?
options: A table with no time labels

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A new sample is skewed by one extreme value, and the question asks for the middle half of observations. Which statistic fits?

items.title: Starting check: classify a shared offset
items.prompt: A thermometer reads 2 degrees Celsius too high for every calibration bath. Which error is most directly indicated?

items.title: Guided practice: identify random scatter
items.prompt: Repeated readings of a stable voltage are 4.8, 5.2, 4.9, and 5.1 volts around a 5.0-volt reference. Which description fits best?

items.title: Less help: repetition and bias
items.prompt: A scale is miscalibrated and reads every mass 5 grams high. What is the best effect of taking 100 repeated readings without recalibration?
options: The mean remains about 5 grams high
The true mass becomes exactly known
The readings become random around truth

items.title: Solo practice: bound significance
items.prompt: A reported difference is statistically significant at the study’s stated threshold. Which conclusion is warranted from that statement alone?
options: Data are less compatible with the null
The result will replicate in every setting

items.title: Near exit: distinguish error types
items.prompt: Measurements vary widely above and below a reference, but their average is close to the reference. Which pattern is most evident?

items.title: Changed exit: interpret an interval
items.prompt: An estimated mean difference is 3 units with a confidence interval from 1 to 5 units. Which statement is most appropriately bounded?
options: The true effect is exactly 3 units
Every future sample must show an increase
The procedure’s interval lies above zero

items.title: Repair: use direction and scatter
items.prompt: All readings cluster tightly 4 units below a certified reference. Which error pattern should be named first?
options: No error because spread is small

items.title: Fresh re-entry: classify new readings
items.prompt: A pipette delivers 9.2, 10.8, 9.5, and 10.5 milliliters around a 10.0-milliliter target. Which feature is most apparent?

items.title: Repair: preserve interval uncertainty
items.prompt: A confidence interval for a difference spans from -2 to 4 units. Which statement avoids overclaiming?

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A new estimate is 8 units with an interval from 6 to 10 units. Which claim is supported without adding practical or causal meaning?
options: The effect is important in practice

items.title: Starting check: association versus cause
items.prompt: In an observational sample, higher sleep duration is associated with higher quiz scores. Which conclusion is supported?
options: Sleep duration and scores were associated
More sleep caused every score increase
All students need a sleep policy

items.title: Guided practice: match claim to result
items.prompt: A controlled comparison shows group X had a lower mean reaction time than group Y under the tested condition. Which conclusion is directly supported?
options: X is faster in every possible setting
Group X had the lower tested mean
The condition explains all human reaction time
Group Y should be excluded from testing

items.title: Less help: retain an alternative
items.prompt: Neighborhoods with more trees report lower summer temperatures, but tree cover was not assigned. Which conclusion is best bounded?
options: Trees alone caused the lower temperatures
All cities must adopt one planting rule

items.title: Solo practice: reject overreach
items.prompt: A treatment group improved by 3 points on one measured outcome compared with control. No other outcomes were measured. Which claim is supported?
options: The treatment improved every relevant outcome
The treatment has no possible adverse effects

items.title: Near exit: choose the strongest bounded claim
items.prompt: Under the tested conditions, enzyme activity rose as substrate concentration increased from 1 to 4 millimolar. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Activity rose across the tested range
Activity rises without limit at all concentrations
Substrate caused every change in the sample
The enzyme should be used clinically

items.title: Changed exit: preserve alternatives
items.prompt: Two schools using a new schedule have higher attendance than two schools using the old schedule, but the schools also differ in transit access. Which conclusion is best?
options: The schedule alone caused higher attendance
Transit access had no possible influence
Every school should adopt the schedule

items.title: Repair: remove the unsupported clause
items.prompt: Result: plants under blue light grew taller than plants under red light for 14 days. Which conclusion removes unsupported scope?
options: Blue light always maximizes all plant growth
Blue-light plants were taller at day 14
All growers should use only blue light

items.title: Fresh re-entry: bound a new result
items.prompt: A new trial finds a lower mean pulse rate in condition A than B during a five-minute observation. Which conclusion is supported?
options: B causes every high pulse reading
Condition A should replace all alternatives
Mean pulse was lower in A during testing

items.title: Repair: keep the alternative visible
items.prompt: Result: neighborhoods with a weekly market show more foot traffic, but they are also closer to transit stops. Which conclusion is bounded?
options: Markets alone caused all added traffic

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A new data set links rehearsal frequency with performance ratings, but prior experience also differs across participants. Which conclusion fits?
options: Prior experience had no possible role
All performers need one rehearsal quota

items.title: Starting check: predict a repeat
items.prompt: Mean output is 20 units at setting A and 31 units at setting B. A new trial repeats setting B under similar conditions. Which prediction is most bounded?
options: Mean output may again be near 31 units

items.title: Guided practice: stay within range
items.prompt: A graph shows response rising from doses 1 to 2 to 3 milligrams. Which implication is supported for a repeat at 2 milligrams?
options: A response above every future dose
An exact response for every participant
A response near the prior 2-mg mean

items.title: Less help: avoid unbounded extension
items.prompt: Accuracy rises across 5, 10, and 15 practice trials. Which prediction is not supported by those data alone?
options: A repeat at 10 trials may resemble the prior mean
A repeat may show sampling variation
The observed range shows an upward pattern

items.title: Solo practice: changed-condition implication
items.prompt: A treatment effect appeared only when temperature stayed below 20 degrees Celsius. A new trial runs at 28 degrees. Which implication is best?
options: The effect must be identical at 28 degrees
The effect may change at 28 degrees

items.title: Near exit: bounded replication
items.prompt: A table shows mean recall of 12 words after a 20-minute delay in three comparable samples. What is the most bounded prediction for a fourth comparable sample?
options: Mean recall may be near 12 words

items.title: Changed exit: alter one condition
items.prompt: A pattern links brighter light with faster growth when water is constant. In a new condition, water becomes severely limited. Which implication is best?
options: Brightness must preserve the same growth gain
The pattern may change under low water

items.title: Repair: use approximate replication language
items.prompt: A prior sample averaged 40 units under condition C. Which prediction for a comparable repeat is appropriately bounded?
options: The repeat mean may be near 40 units
The repeat must be exactly 40 units

items.title: Fresh re-entry: predict a new repeat
items.prompt: A new set of comparable trials averages 7.5 seconds at setting D. What is a bounded prediction for another D trial set?
options: Its mean may be near 7.5 seconds
Setting D should replace all settings

items.title: Repair: identify the altered link
items.prompt: Performance improved with feedback when practice occurred daily. A new group practices monthly. Which implication is best?
options: Feedback must have the identical effect

items.title: Fresh changed re-entry
items.prompt: A new pattern shows lower noise improves detection when signal strength is fixed. A later trial weakens the signal. Which projection is bounded?
options: Signal strength has no possible role
All devices should use one setting
The gain may change with weaker signal
